chunks: “Allah, Mighty and Majestic, only made zakat twenty-five dirhams in every thousand because He, Mighty and Majestic, created the creation, so He knew their rich and their poor, their strong and their weak. Thus He made from every thousand twenty-five needy ones. Were it not for that, Allah would have increased it for them, because He is their Creator and He knows them best.”

key_terms.أَعْلَمُ بِهِمْ: most knowing of them, fully aware of their realities and needs
key_terms.الزَّكَاةَ: zakat, the obligatory alms-tax prescribed on wealth
key_terms.خَالِقُهُمْ: their Creator, Allah as the One who brought them into existence
key_terms.دِرْهَماً: dirhams, the monetary measure mentioned for the zakat amount
key_terms.غَنِيَّهُمْ: their wealthy people, those possessing financial means
key_terms.فَقِيرَهُمْ: their poor people, those lacking sufficient means
key_terms.مِسْكِيناً: a needy person, one in a state of need and deprivation

ai.seo_question: Why did Allah prescribe zakat as twenty-five dirhams for every thousand?
ai.summary: This hadith explains the measure of zakat as established by Allah, based on His perfect knowledge of His creation and their differing conditions of wealth, poverty, strength, and weakness. It presents the obligation as divinely proportioned with wisdom and justice, since Allah is the Creator and knows best what suffices for His servants.

en.bab-ul-qaim-publications: Hadith.1582 - Imam Jafar ibn Muhammad Al-Sadiq (as) said:

"Allah (swt), the Almighty and Majestic, has prescribed Zakat as twenty-five dirhams for every thousand because He created the creation and knew their wealthy and their poor, their strong and their weak. He allocated from every thousand an amount sufficient for twenty-five poor individuals. If this were not sufficient, Allah (swt) would have increased it, for He is their Creator and knows them best."
